expectations.text: Produces complete, self-contained working code for the described task
expectations.evidence: HttpError thrown from validation blocks and transaction callbacks without handler-level try-catch; relies on external error middleware not shown

expectations.text: Requires an idempotency key as a parameter rather than making it optional
expectations.evidence: idempotencyKeySchema.safeParse() with 400 response if not present

expectations.text: Backs idempotency with a database unique constraint, not application logic alone
expectations.evidence: @@unique([orderId, idempotencyKey]) in schema; CREATE UNIQUE INDEX in migration

expectations.text: Uses distinct types for the identifiers rather than bare strings for both order and refund ids
expectations.evidence: Uses z.string().uuid() validation but no branded types or type aliases

expectations.text: Handles money as integer minor units rather than a float
Validates the refund amount server-side against the order rather than trusting the caller
expectations.evidence: Aggregates PENDING/requires_action/SUCCEEDED refunds, computes remainingCents, throws 422 if exceeded

expectations.text: Scopes the write so one tenant or user cannot refund another's order
expectations.evidence: RLS policy uses EXISTS check to verify orderId belongs to Order with correct tenantId; transaction sets app.tenant_id

expectations.text: Closes by naming which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: tenant RLS prevents cross-tenant refunds, locked order row and reserved-refund aggregate prevent over-refunds, idempotency key prevents duplicates

expectations.text: Names at least one thing it deliberately left possible and why
expectations.evidence: Stripe webhook should update status for async failures/cancellations; keeping pending refunds reserved is the safe default until reconciliation
